turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... I just can’t stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. It's really bothering me. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just don't see it that way. I feel like it’s the very first thing the families I work for, or the nurses, or even the people at my church notice when they look at me. I just can't stop focusing on it, and I don't know what to do.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes an obsessive focus on a perceived flaw (sagging, uneven spot around the jaw and neck) that others tell them looks normal, which is the core feature of preoccupation with appearance.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself performing any specific actions, such as constantly checking the mirror, touching the area, or seeking reassurance from others, to try to deal with how you feel about your jaw and neck?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Especially before I leave for work or a meeting. I just... I keep going back to the bathroom mirror. I'll stand there fixing my collar and trying to arrange my hair around my neck to hide it. And then, even after I walk away, I'll pull out my phone and take another look in the camera just to check it again. 

Sometimes I ask my daughter if it looks strange, too. Honestly, doing all that... it's actually made me late more than once.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors related to their appearance concerns, including repeatedly checking mirrors and phone cameras, adjusting clothing and hair to hide their neck, and seeking reassurance from their daughter.

turns.doctor_question: How much does this constant checking and worrying about your appearance impact your ability to get through your day or interact with the people around you?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it gets in the way more than I'd like to admit. At work, I've actually passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on supervisory roles. I just... I worry too much that people will be staring right at my face and neck the whole time. And I've fallen behind on my paperwork, too, because I get stuck in the bathroom trying to make myself look presentable before I can focus on anything else. 

It affects my personal life, too. I've stopped going to my book club and my walking group lately. It just feels like too much work to get ready and try to hide it, so I just stay home instead.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient expresses excessive worry that others will stare at their face and neck, indicating a preoccupation with their appearance.
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes getting stuck in the bathroom trying to make themselves look presentable and putting significant effort into hiding their perceived flaws.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever sought out or considered any medical, surgical, or cosmetic procedures to fix your jaw or neck?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't. I mean, I've never gone to a doctor or a surgeon about it. I haven't looked into any kind of surgery or procedures like that to fix it. I just try to cover it up myself.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms trying to cover up their perceived flaws (excessive camouflaging), which is a subtype of appearance-related repetitive behaviors, even though they deny seeking cosmetic procedures.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever find yourself picking, scratching, or rubbing your skin in that area to try and smooth it out or make it look better?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really do that. I mean, I might touch my neck sometimes just to adjust my collar or my hair, like I mentioned, but I don't sit there picking at the skin or rubbing it to try and smooth it out. It's more about trying to cover the shape of it, not changing the skin itself.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient denies skin picking but confirms engaging in other appearance-related repetitive behaviors, specifically camouflaging by adjusting their collar or hair to cover the shape of their neck.

turns.doctor_question: When you worry that people are staring at your jaw or neck, do you feel that they are judging you specifically because of how that area looks, or are you more generally worried about being embarrassed or scrutinized in social situations?
turns.patient_response: I think it's specifically about my jaw and neck. I mean, I don't really get nervous just from being around people or talking to them. It's really just that I'm convinced they're looking right at that part of my face and thinking how awful it looks. If I didn't have this problem with my jaw and neck, I don't think I'd be worried about being judged at all.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms a specific preoccupation with their jaw and neck, believing others are staring at it and judging it as awful.
